messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Renewal insurance clearance — uplift variance & price protection (BluePeak)

Team — initiating a short escalation for exec clearance on a large, strategic multi-year request from BluePeak Health (contact: Ella Thompson). Key facts up front:
- Deal snapshot: 3-year committed deployment (starts Jan 1, 2028) with strong year-over-year consumption growth: projected billings $2.1M (Y1) -> $4.6M (Y2) -> $7.0M (Y3) per the attached model.
- Ask from customer: 3-year price lock (no price increases for term), uplift cap for renewals set at 10% annually, and a hard guarantee that renewal increases for year 4 cannot exceed 15% (they want an explicit renewal-protection clause).
- What Deal Desk is requesting from Execs: an exception to our standard uplift guardrails. Specifically, they want a 0% price movement during term and a renewal cap that effectively reduces our default flexibility. Deal desk suggests a commercial package with a slightly higher uplift cap (they asked for a 10% cap; they will accept a 15% cap) but are asking for our approval to commit to these protections.

Why this matters: BluePeak is an early vertical reference (healthcare analytics) with potential for significant expansion and referrals into two enterprise accounts. They also plan to move sensitive workloads to a Private deployment, which increases switching cost once live. Approving a stronger renewal protection here sets precedent but materially helps close and expand.

Proposal for Exec consideration (attached: BP-term-sheet-v3.pdf, financial-model-bluepeak.xlsx, redline_term_sheet.docx):
1) Approve 3-year price lock (no baseline price increases inside the 3-year term).
2) Allow an uplift-cap exception: cap renewal uplift at +15% at each annual renewal during the term, and cap first post-term renewal (year 4) at +20%. This is above our typical guardrail (25% max uplift over multiyear anchoring) — request permission to proceed.
3) Require minimum annual consumption thresholds (committed MRR floors) and a 60-day true-up; include a rollback clause if consumption falls below thresholds >2 consecutive quarters.
4) Escrow-style protection: customer places a portion of year 1 prepayment into a contingent escrow to offset early termination risk.

Requested approval deadline: COB Nov 22 (we have legal redlines from BluePeak and procurement pressure). If approved, I will finalize term language and loop Legal/Finance for signatures.

Thanks — Jonas

Subject: Re: Request: Renewal insurance clearance — uplift variance & price protection (BluePeak)

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the attached packet. Quick Deal Desk read (high level):
- Commercially, BluePeak is a strong reference and the retention benefit is real. We can support a narrower uplift cap than their ask (15% per year) provided we put explicit guardrails in place.
- Recommended conditional concessions: 1) require a 12-month minimum contractual consumption per year (MRR floor), 2) include a 60-day true-up/usage reconciliation tied to billings, and 3) add a mid-term revert clause if utilization deviates >40% vs forecast for two consecutive quarters.
- For precedent control, we should include a one-time documented approval with exact language and limit this to this named counterparty and any corporate affiliates; no broad policy change. Deal Desk will prepare an approval memo for Exec signature if Leadership greenlights the numbers below.

Suggested finalized package to propose to Execs:
- 3-year price lock (no increases during term)
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% per year (first post-term renewal max +20%)
- Minimum annual consumption floors and 60-day true-up
- Mid-term performance revert clause (two-quarter trigger)
- Escrow holdback of 10% of first-year committed spend until 12 months in production

I attached inline comments in redline_term_sheet.docx; see highlights on Sections 4–6 for the revert/true-up language. If Execs approve in principle, Deal Desk will craft the final sign-off memo to be countersigned by Legal + Finance.

— Jordan

Subject: Re: Request: Renewal insurance clearance — uplift variance & price protection (BluePeak)

Circling with Finance view — high level:
- P&L impact: if we lock prices for 3 years and cap renewals at 15%/20%, upside is capped while usage could exceed forecasts given LLM token growth; this increases unit-cost exposure. The attached model (financial-model-bluepeak.xlsx) shows a downside if year-3 usage is 25%+ above forecast without commensurate price re-opener.
- Conditions Finance requires for signoff: 1) a higher on-paper floor for year 1 revenue recognition (protects accounting), 2) commitment to a minimum effective blended ARR floor across the three years (not just MRR floors), and 3) a true-up tied to a pre-agreed token-band pricing schedule so marginal usage beyond forecast is billed at a premium band (instead of absorbing at committed rate).
- If Execs want to proceed as-is, Finance recommends we add a 6–9 month scheduled review with the customer tied to a performance-based price cadence so we can adjust movement banding if necessary.

I think the Deal Desk package is reasonable from a go-to-market perspective but we should explicitly require the token-band true-up and the blended ARR floor to reduce our downside. Please see the short ROI worksheet I added to the model under the 'FinanceNotes' tab. This needs Exec-level approval because it establishes a pricing precedent for the health vertical.

Subject: Exec escalation: BluePeak renewal-insurance approval request (decision needed)

Laura/Markus — forwarding the short chain and ask for formal Exec signoff. TL;DR: BluePeak (healthcare analytics) requests a three-year price lock and explicit renewal protection that limits uplift. Deal Desk + Finance have aligned to a conditional package; Legal will redline language after your direction. The recommended package for your approval is below — please reply with the single-letter approval code (A/B/C) by EOD Wed Nov 24 so I can finalize language with the customer.

Recommended package (Deal Desk + Finance conditional):
A) Full approval (preferred by Sales):
   - 3-year price lock (no increases inside the term)
   - Renewal uplift cap: 15% per year during term; first post-term renewal cap +20%
   - Minimum blended ARR floor across 3 years (Finance to define exact $s)
   - Token-band true-up: marginal usage above forecast billed at premium band defined in attached model
   - Escrow holdback: 10% of Year 1 committed spend to cover early termination risk
   - Mid-term revert clause: triggers if utilization deviates >40% for two consecutive quarters

B) Conditional approval (lower risk):
   - 3-year price lock only if customer accepts a 5% annual uplift right (protects us) and the token-band true-up; no escrow requirement waived

C) Decline (if risk too high):
   - Return to customer with standard guardrails: no multi-year price lock; offer 12-month firm term with a 25% uplift cap at renewal

Why we need Execs: this creates a named exception that changes precedent for vertical deals and affects our long-term unit economics. Deal economics are favorable if BluePeak hits forecast, and the reference value for our healthcare vertical is high. Approving Option A commits Redwood to a meaningful price rigidity; approving B is a safer middle ground.

Please indicate A/B/C by reply or use the embedded HubSpot approval link (HubSpot ID in related_links). If you need a one-pager for the board/exec forum, I can prepare.

Thanks — Jonas
